messages.author: e302709dad51d37a
messages.subject: Use vector element in set_source
parts:
Hi,

I am having some trouble setting the source for my generator - I want to use the ith element of a vector as the frequency at which to generate arrivals, but I keep getting the following error:

Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) : 
  Evaluation error: there is no arrival running.

Here is the code which is causing the error:

set_source('gallon_', function() batch_speeds[get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number')]) %>%

I am confused because I can use the get_attribute function as the vector index in a log statement and it works fine:

log_(function() toString(paste0('Batch #', get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number'), ' finished: ', batch_nums[get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number')], '\n'))) %>%

Any thoughts on how to resolve this?

Thanks,
John

parts:
Sure thing - here's some code:

b_index <- function(start){
  l <- start
  function() {
    l <<- l + 1
    return(l)
  }
}

b_num        <- b_index(0)
batch_nums   <- c(10, 20, 30)
batch_speeds <- c(1, 2, 3)
batches      <- c()

for (i in (1:length(batch_nums))){
  batches[i] <- sum(batch_nums[1:i])
}

gallon_line <- simmer()

gallon <-
  trajectory('Gallon path') %>%
    log_('gallon arrived\n') %>%
    set_attribute('index', 1, mod="+") %>%
    branch( function() (get_attribute(gallon_line, 'index') %in% batches)
          , continue = T
          , trajectory() %>%
              set_attribute('batch_number', function() b_num()) %>%
log_(function() toString(paste0('Batch #', get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number'), ' finished: ', batch_nums[get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number')], '\n'))) %>%

#set_source('gallon_', function() batch_speeds[get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number')]) %>%
              deactivate('gallon_') %>%
              timeout(10) %>%
              activate('gallon_')) %>%
    log_('gallon finished\n')

gallon_line <-
  simmer('fill line') %>%
  add_generator('gallon_', gallon, function() .025, mon = 2) %>%
  run(until = 5)


Let me know if you have any questions.

John

2018-05-22 22:00 GMT+02:00 John Redmond <john.re...@gmail.com>:
> Okay, is it possible to call a vector element in the set_source function?

I'm not sure what you mean by that. The rules are simple: set_source
substitutes the source of arrivals. In the case of a generator
(add_generator), you must provide a function, because it substitutes
the generation function ("function() 0.025" in your example), which
must return interarrival times. In the case of a data source
(add_dataframe), you must provide a data frame, because it substitutes
the one provided in the first place.

Iñaki

I was able to find a solution, although I am almost sure it's not what you would consider a best practice.

I am using a generator, so I am required to pass a function for the set_source method... Since I could not use the set_attribute method for setting the arrival's source (because there was no arrival running) I decided to set up a dummy resource and use the set_capacity/get_capacity functions to index my array of varying generator speeds (since the capacity functions are not arrival-dependent).

This is what I'm doing (the setting is a changeover for paint batches on a gallon line):

set_capacity('batch_counter', function() b_num()) %>%
deactivate('gallon_') %>%

timeout(22) %>%
set_source('gallon_', function() batch_speeds[get_capacity(gallon_line,'batch_counter')]) %>%
activate('gallon_')

b_num() is a closure that serves to index the current batch number.

Just wanted to follow up,
John

> Okay, is it possible to call a vector element in the set_source function?

I'm not sure what you mean by that. The rules are simple: set_source
substitutes the source of arrivals. In the case of a generator
(add_generator), you must provide a function, because it substitutes
the generation function ("function() 0.025" in your example), which
must return interarrival times. In the case of a data source
(add_dataframe), you must provide a data frame, because it substitutes
the one provided in the first place.

Iñaki

Error in run_(private$sim_obj, until) :

Here is the code which is causing the error:

set_source('gallon_', function() batch_speeds[get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number')]) %>%

I am confused because I can use the get_attribute function as the vector index in a log statement and it works fine:

log_(function() toString(paste0('Batch #', get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number'), ' finished: ', batch_nums[get_attribute(gallon_line,'batch_number')], '\n'))) %>%

Any thoughts on how to resolve this?

Thanks,
John
